measurement.name: Pacific Equatorial Undercurrent
measurement.range_interpretation: One approximate regional background value; no numerical uncertainty, range, confidence interval, annual extrema or seasonal observations supplied.
measurement.geographic_scope: Pacific eastward equatorial subsurface jet; background approximation without a fixed section longitude or paired edge coordinates. Not the generic cross-basin family or Atlantic/Indian EUC.
measurement.section_orientation: No reproducible transverse section endpoints supplied for the regional breadth description.
measurement.layer: Subsurface current background; adjacent approximate thickness and 50–200 m core depths are context, not a fixed width measurement layer.
measurement.time_convention: Background synthesis in a 2022 article; no dated width occupation or monthly width climatology. Simulation years and transport/velocity climatologies have different support.
measurement.boundary_rule: Author-reported approximate background width. No velocity cutoff, paired boundaries or explicit transverse section extracted. Model transport boxes are not width boundaries.
measurement.source_citation: Wang et al. (2022), Wind-Driven Mechanisms for the Variations of the Pacific Equatorial Undercurrent Based on Adjoint Sensitivity Analysis, Frontiers in Marine Science 9:908939, doi:10.3389/fmars.2022.908939.
measurement.source_locator: Introduction opening paragraph, printed p1 (PDF page 1); different model/transport supports in sections 2.1–2.2 and Figures 1/2, printed pp3–4.
measurement.extraction_method: Approximate width transcribed from visually inspected publisher original p1 prose; no map, current axis or model transport-box width digitization.
measurement.source_quality_note: Original publisher p1 width and p4 transport/velocity context visually inspected. Background 400 km is not a derived width from the adjoint experiment. Underlying historical width method and exact attribution remain unreviewed.
remaining_gates: Resolve the original historical width support and paired boundary method.
